$comment: The (table, column) pairs that role `authenticated` is permitted to UPDATE
in schema `public`. Anything the database actually permits but that is not
listed here is a finding, and the gate fails.
`anon` must have NO update surface at all. There is no anon list: any anon
Rationale for the shape of this file: RLS is row-level and cannot express
'this user may write these columns'. Column-level GRANTs can. So the real
control surface is (table grants) x (column grants) x (UPDATE/ALL policies),
and that product is what the gate derives and diffs against this list.
Adding a pair here is a security decision. It means: a normal signed-in
user, calling PostgREST directly with the public anon key and their own
JWT, may set this column on any row their RLS policies expose. Do not add
a column merely because some API route writes it -- API routes can use a
SECURITY DEFINER RPC or the service role instead.

$comment_users: DENY role            -- C-1 privilege escalation; /api/team owns role changes.
DENY email           -- identity is owned by auth.users.
DENY updated_at      -- maintained by trigger update_users_updated_at.
DENY full_name       -- NOT derived, but no authenticated path writes it:
set once at signup, read as a legacy fallback.
$comment_organizations: authority. Stripe webhook (service role) and the admin DEFINER RPCs only.
DENY stripe_customer_id -- set by the webhook.
DENY feature_flags      -- set_feature_flag() only, super-admin gated.
server claim flags; a client write breaks the claim guard.
DENY siret              -- company registration identity, not a preference.
DENY updated_at         -- maintained by trigger update_organizations_updated_at.
DENY id, slug, created_at, pilot_notes -- identity or staff-only.
$comment_subscriptions: EMPTY BY DESIGN. No column of this table may be written by a normal
session. licensed_capacity, status, plan_id, current_period_end and the
stripe_* columns are all billing authority (C-2), written by the webhook
under the service role. The capacity route calls Stripe and then persists
server-side; it does not need client UPDATE.
$comment_assets: Wide by necessity: the asset edit/archive/retire modals write these
directly from the browser today (H-2). This list documents the CURRENT
surface so the gate is meaningful now; H-2's fix is to move these writes
behind API routes, after which most of these pairs should be removed.
NOT is_demo_data: feeds the billable asset count.
$comment_rest: no authenticated UPDATE surface at all. Omitted deliberately -- an empty
or absent list means zero permitted pairs.
